A summary that fits the video

Keep the details
that matter.

A recipe needs quantities. A review needs tradeoffs. Clipse chooses a summary approach that fits the video, and you can edit what each category preserves.

20 editable categories + an Other fallback

Recipes

Ingredients, quantities, temperatures, and cooking times stated in the captions.

Tutorials

Prerequisites, ordered steps, settings, and the mistakes worth avoiding.

Reviews

Testing conditions, strengths, weaknesses, and who a product suits.

Interviews

The main ideas, who said what, and the qualifications that change the meaning.

A little clarity about your data

Your library stays
with you.

Keys and saved summaries live in your Chrome profile. Captions go directly to OpenAI to create a summary. If you enable Jev classification, excerpts also go to TypeSafe.

Before you begin

A few useful answers.

What do I need to use Clipse?

Chrome 116 or later, an OpenAI API key with access to your selected model and available API credit, and a YouTube video with readable captions. An OpenAI API account is billed separately from a ChatGPT subscription. Install Clipse from the Chrome Web Store.

Does it work without opening the video?

Yes. Hover over a YouTube thumbnail and click Summarize. Clipse tries to read captions while keeping you on the current page. If needed, it uses a temporary muted background video tab for extraction.

Can I choose the language and level of detail?

Choose your preferred caption language, summary language, and brief or detailed length in Settings. Availability depends on the caption tracks YouTube provides.

What happens to my saved summaries?

They remain in this Chrome profile. Search them, reopen them, copy them as Markdown, or export and import a JSON backup. Keys are excluded from backups. You can delete individual summaries or clear your saved history.

Do I need Jev or a TypeSafe account?

No. OpenAI handles classification and summarization by default. Jev is an optional classifier that requires a separate TypeSafe key; OpenAI still writes the summary.

How accurate are the summaries?

Clipse works from captions, which can contain errors or leave out information shown on screen. AI summaries can also make mistakes. Use the timestamped source to check important details.
